summary: Parkevtate Vosianc compares Amazon and Uber head-to-head to decide his fourth-best stock to buy in November, restating his top three as Meta Platforms first, Nvidia second and Netflix third. On earnings growth, Uber leads with analysts forecasting over 30% earnings-per-share growth each year for several years, versus over 23.4% for Amazon, and both have seen estimates revised higher in 2026. Uber also has the better operating margin at 14% versus 13.3% for Amazon and has improved margins more dramatically, though Amazon's AWS margins approach 40% — at least three times the rest of the company — and he expects Amazon's overall margin could approach 20% within five years as AWS grows. Uber's asset-light model, with drivers as contractors rather than employees, drives far higher revenue per employee and easier growth, but each ride or delivery carries a driver cost. Driverless technology is both a risk from Tesla and Google's Waymo and an opportunity, since removing driver pay could cut a major expense. On valuation, Amazon trades at 25 times forward earnings versus 16 times for Uber, and his discounted cash flow values are $365 for Amazon against $272 today and $110 for Uber against $70 — roughly 30% and 50% undervalued after a margin of safety. Calls: AMZN BUY at $272, fair value $365, ranked fourth; UBER BUY at $70, fair value $110, ranked fifth, closely behind, because Amazon's moat is stronger and more durable even though Uber looks cheaper.
